Where a Univariate Family Starts, From the Data

Source: R/starting_values.R
start_from_moments.Rd

Returns n_start starting values whose first is computed from the response and whose rest are random draws. Both continuous_distrib and discrete_distrib register this method, so a univariate family uses it unless the family registers a method of its own, as pig1_distrib(), pig2_distrib(), zero_adjusted() and zero_inflated() do.

The data-based value comes from moment_estimates() where the family has an entry there. The other families fall back to reading params_interpretation: a parameter meaning a location is started at the sample median, one meaning a spread at the sample standard deviation or its square, one meaning degrees of freedom at what the sample kurtosis implies, and a shape, a dispersion or a probability keeps its draw, because those are of order one whatever the data.

Usage

start_from_moments(distrib, y, n_start = 5L, ...)

Arguments

distrib

A univariate distribution, supplying params, params_interpretation and params_bounds.

y

The response, a numeric vector. Non-finite entries are dropped, and a sample with fewer than two usable values yields only the random draws.

n_start

The number of starting values, a single positive integer. Defaults to 5, and a value below 1 is raised to 1.

...

Unused.

Value

A list of n_start named parameter lists on the parameter scale, the first from the data where one could be computed.

Why the base method is not used for univariate families

The base method draws each parameter from its own domain and does not read y. That is adequate while the response is of order one and fails when it is not: on a response of mean 919 and standard deviation 169 the draws are of order one, the first Newton step is taken where the residuals are hundreds of standard deviations wide, and the scale can run to the largest representable double. A start computed from the data is on the scale of the data.

Degrees of freedom from the kurtosis

A \(t\) of \(\nu\) degrees has excess kurtosis \(6/(\nu-4)\), so a sample kurtosis above 0.05 inverts to \(\nu = 6/\hat\gamma_2 + 4\), capped at 100; a sample no heavier-tailed than a Gaussian starts at 30. A large start keeps a student_t2, whose scale parameter is the standard deviation, away from the degenerate ridge at its lower bound of \(\nu = 2\), where the scale tends to infinity as \(\nu\) falls; a run started at a small \(\nu\) can follow the ridge down to the bound.

Bounds and the remaining starts

Every value is moved strictly inside its parameter's bounds before it is returned, because a sample median can land exactly on the boundary of a support and the validator treats bounds as open. Only the first start is data-based; the rest stay random, so a caller requesting several still explores, and fit_distrib() reaches them when the first fails.

See also

moment_estimates() for the family-by-family inversions; distrib_start() for the generic; clamp_to_bounds() for the boundary rule of the moment estimates; fit_distrib(), which consumes the list.
